text: Write a program that demonstrates scope: an inner block's variable is invisible outside it. Fill in the two blanks so the program compiles and prints what the comments claim.
choices: ___;                            // declare a variable in the inner block
System.out.println(outer + inner);   // prints 3 -- inner sees outer
// System.out.println(inner);       // would not compile: out of scope
explanation: Verified: 3 then 1. Scope is a compile-time rule about where a name is visible, and the commented line is the whole demonstration — uncomment it and the program does not build. Chapter 25 implements this rule in nine lines: look in the local map, then ask the parent, and the search order *is* shadowing. Reverse the two clauses and parameters stop working.
